$$
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the trigonometric identity 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identity is

$$
\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}.
$$

Now, we rewrite the integral using the above identity, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-\operatorname{cosh}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{0}+{e}^{-0}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2+{2}^{-1}}{2}-\frac{1+1}{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}-1 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
